examples.en: We built a bonfire at the campsite and talked.

examples.ko: 추운 밤에 화톳불 앞에 모여 손을 녹였어요.
examples.en: On the cold night we gathered in front of the bonfire and warmed our hands.
The bonfire blazed up and lit the surroundings.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 축제 날 밤마다 화톳불 주위에서 춤을 춰요.
examples.en: On festival nights the villagers dance around the bonfire.
The children roasted sweet potatoes in the bonfire and ate them.

examples.ko: 바람이 불자 화톳불의 불꽃이 크게 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: When the wind blew, the flames of the bonfire swayed wildly.

explain: '모닥불'과 비슷한 말이에요. 캠핑에서는 '모닥불을 피우다'라고 많이 말하고, 화톳불도 같은 동사 '피우다'와 함께 써요. 불이 타오르는 모습은 '활활'과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a close relative of '모닥불' (campfire). At campsites people often say '모닥불을 피우다', and 화톳불 is also used with the verb '피우다' (to light a fire). The adverb '활활' (blazing) goes well with it.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 성격이 화통해서 같이 일하기 편해요.
examples.en: Our team leader is open and straightforward, so it's easy to work with them.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말도 행동도 참 화통해요.
examples.en: That person is really frank and decisive in both words and actions.

examples.ko: 화통한 성격 덕분에 친구가 정말 많아요.
examples.en: Thanks to a big-hearted personality, I have a lot of friends.
My older brother generously paid for the meal first without hesitating.

examples.ko: 화통하게 사과하니까 다들 금방 마음이 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Because he apologized so openly, everyone softened right away.

examples.ko: 사장님이 화통하셔서 가격을 많이 깎아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner was so generous that they gave me a big discount.

explain: '시원시원하다'처럼 성격이 막힘없고 털털하고 솔직할 때 써요. 주로 사람의 성격을 좋게 말할 때 쓰고, '화통한 성격', '화통하게 쓰다/사과하다'처럼 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '소심하다', '쩨쩨하다'예요.
explain_en: Like '시원시원하다', it describes someone with an open, easygoing, honest personality. It is mostly a compliment for people, as in '화통한 성격' or '화통하게 사과하다'. Opposite feelings are expressed by '소심하다' (timid) or '쩨쩨하다' (stingy, petty).

examples.en: The family gathered on the holiday and played hwatu.
My grandmother really loves playing hwatu.

examples.ko: 화투 한 벌을 사서 친구들과 놀았어요.
examples.en: I bought a set of hwatu cards and played with my friends.

examples.ko: 이 화투에는 꽃과 동물 그림이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: These hwatu cards have pictures of flowers and animals.
To play Go-Stop, you need hwatu cards.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 화투로 재미 삼아 점을 보세요.
examples.en: My grandfather tells fortunes with hwatu cards just for fun.

explain: 서양 카드는 '카드 게임', 화투는 '화투를 치다'처럼 동사 '치다'와 함께 말해요. '고스톱'이 화투로 하는 대표적인 게임이에요. 돈을 걸면 도박이 될 수 있어서, 말할 때 분위기를 살펴요.
explain_en: With playing cards you say '카드 게임', but with hwatu the verb is '치다', as in '화투를 치다'. Go-Stop is the best-known game played with hwatu. Betting money can turn it into gambling, so pay attention to the setting when you mention it.

examples.en: The painter captured the autumn scenery on canvas.

examples.ko: 이 화폭 안에는 작은 마을이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: A small village is painted within this canvas.

examples.ko: 큰 화폭 가득 붉은 노을이 펼쳐졌어요.
examples.en: A red sunset spread across the whole large canvas.

examples.ko: 그는 어릴 적 고향을 화폭에 옮겼어요.
examples.en: He transferred his childhood hometown onto canvas.

examples.ko: 화폭이 너무 커서 혼자 옮기기 어려워요.
examples.en: The canvas is so big that it's hard to move alone.
At the exhibition, I felt a different color in every canvas.

explain: '캔버스'는 외래어이고, 화폭은 그림이 그려지는 화면 전체를 말해요. '화폭에 담다'처럼 그림으로 그려 낸다는 느낌으로 많이 써요. 대화에서는 '그림'이라고 해도 충분해요.
explain_en: '캔버스' is a loanword, while 화폭 is the whole surface on which a picture is painted. It is often used in '화폭에 담다' (to capture on canvas). In everyday talk, just saying '그림' (picture) is also enough.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 화훼 농가가 많기로 유명해요.
examples.en: This area is famous for its many flower farms.
A spring flower festival is held at the flower complex.
Flower consumption dropped sharply this year.

examples.ko: 졸업식 철에는 화훼 시장이 아주 붐벼요.
examples.en: During graduation season, the flower market is very crowded.

examples.ko: 그는 화훼 산업을 공부하려고 대학에 갔어요.
examples.en: He went to university to study the flower industry.
I bought flowers cheaply at the flower wholesale market.

explain: 꽃이나 화초를 키우고 파는 일과 관련해서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. '화훼 농가', '화훼 시장', '화훼 산업'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 써요. 꽃 한 송이를 가리킬 때는 그냥 '꽃'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word used about growing and selling flowers and ornamental plants. It usually comes before another noun, as in '화훼 농가', '화훼 시장' and '화훼 산업'. For a single flower, people just say '꽃'.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 세계 랭킹 1위 자리가 확고부동해요.
examples.en: That player's spot at number one in the world rankings is unshakable.
My decision is firm, so please don't try to stop me.

examples.ko: 저는 확고부동한 원칙이 있어서 흔들리지 않아요.
examples.en: I have firm principles, so I don't waver.
That team is the undisputed number one in the league.

examples.ko: 어려움 속에서도 두 사람의 믿음은 확고부동했어요.
examples.en: Even in hard times, the two people's trust was unshakable.

examples.ko: 그는 끝까지 확고부동하게 자기 입장을 지켰어요.
examples.en: He firmly held his position to the end.

explain: '확고하다'와 비슷하지만 더 강하고 딱딱해서 뉴스나 연설에서 잘 나와요. '확고부동한 1위', '확고부동한 입장'처럼 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '확고하다'나 '흔들림이 없다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '확고하다' but stronger and more formal, so it often appears in news and speeches. It is used in phrases like '확고부동한 1위' and '확고부동한 입장'. In everyday talk, '확고하다' or '흔들림이 없다' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 작은 글씨는 확대경으로 봐야 잘 보여요.
examples.en: Small print is only clear when you look through a magnifying glass.
My grandfather reads the newspaper holding a magnifying glass.
In science class we observed leaves with a magnifying glass.

examples.ko: 이 확대경은 열 배까지 크게 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This magnifying glass enlarges things up to ten times.
I found an old magnifying glass in the drawer.

examples.ko: 확대경이 있으면 우표를 자세히 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you have a magnifying glass, you can look at stamps in detail.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '돋보기'라고 더 자주 말해요. 눈에 쓰는 '돋보기안경'은 안경이라서 확대경과 달라요. 확대경은 설명서나 과학 수업에서 볼 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: In daily conversation people more often say '돋보기'. Note that '돋보기안경' means reading glasses worn on the face, which is different from a handheld magnifier. 확대경 is the word you may see in manuals and science classes.

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 그 후보의 승리가 확실시돼요.
examples.en: That candidate's victory in this election looks certain.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 올 것이 확실시된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say rain tomorrow is all but certain.

examples.ko: 우리 팀의 우승이 확실시되자 모두 환호했어요.
examples.en: When our team's win became certain, everyone cheered.
The merger of the two companies is looking certain.
The player who was almost certain to join the national team got injured.

examples.ko: 금리 인상이 확실시되면 주식 시장이 흔들릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If a rate hike becomes certain, the stock market could be shaken.

explain: 뉴스에서 '~이/가 확실시되다'로 많이 나와요. 아직 공식 발표는 없지만 거의 틀림없다는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '거의 확실해요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It often appears in the news as '~이/가 확실시되다'. It means there is no official announcement yet, but it is almost sure. In daily conversation, people say '거의 확실해요' (it's almost certain).

examples.en: I received a firm job commitment from the company.
It's risky to sign a contract without a firm commitment.

examples.ko: 사장님께 월급을 올려 준다는 확약이 왔어요.
examples.en: A firm promise came from the boss that my pay would go up.

examples.ko: 그 투자자는 추가 지원에 대한 확약을 줬어요.
examples.en: That investor gave a firm pledge of additional support.
A pledge made only in words is hard to trust.
The government sent its pledge of support in writing.

explain: '약속'보다 훨씬 딱딱하고, 책임지고 꼭 하겠다는 느낌이 강해요. 계약, 투자, 채용처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 '확약을 받다/주다'로 써요. 친구와의 약속에는 그냥 '약속'을 써요.
explain_en: It is much more formal than '약속' and strongly implies taking responsibility to follow through. It is used in formal settings like contracts, investment and hiring, as in '확약을 받다/주다'. For plans with a friend, just use '약속'.

examples.en: The boss firmly promised to promote me within this year.
If you commit to it in writing, I'll sign the contract right away.

examples.ko: 확약하기 전에 조건을 한 번 더 확인해요.
examples.en: Before making a firm commitment, I check the terms once more.
When the government pledged its support, the residents felt relieved.
No one can guarantee the result.
He gave his firm word that he would take responsibility to the end.

explain: 가벼운 약속은 '약속하다'를 쓰고, 확약하다는 계약이나 공식적인 자리에서 틀림없이 하겠다고 말할 때 써요. '-겠다고 확약하다' 형태가 자주 나와요. '확약해 주다'처럼 상대에게 요청할 때도 써요.
explain_en: For casual promises use '약속하다'; 확약하다 is for saying you will definitely do something in a contract or formal setting. The pattern '-겠다고 확약하다' is common. You can also ask someone with '확약해 주다'.

examples.en: Even the doctor couldn't say for sure whether it would be cured.

examples.ko: 아직은 누가 이길지 확언할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't say for certain yet who will win.
What's your reason for stating it so definitely?
Experts say it is hard to state the cause definitively.
The boss didn't give a definite answer about payday.
He confidently declared that it would succeed.

explain: '확언할 수 없다', '확언하기 어렵다'처럼 부정이나 어려움과 함께 가장 자주 나와요. 뉴스나 인터뷰에서 조심스럽게 말할 때 잘 쓰는 표현이에요. '단언하다'도 비슷하게 쓰이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It most often appears with negation or difficulty, as in '확언할 수 없다' and '확언하기 어렵다'. It is handy in news and interviews when someone is being careful about what they claim. '단언하다' is a similar word.

examples.ko: 새 에어컨을 켜자 방 온도가 확연히 내려갔어요.
examples.en: When I turned on the new air conditioner, the room temperature clearly dropped.

examples.ko: 운동을 시작한 뒤로 체력이 확연히 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: Since I started exercising, my stamina has noticeably improved.
The two twins have clearly different personalities.
When you compare the two photos, the difference is obvious.
I was surprised to see such a clear change.
The result wasn't clear, so they tested again.

explain: 눈에 띄게 뚜렷하다는 뜻으로, 차이나 변화를 말할 때 가장 많이 써요. '확연히 달라지다', '차이가 확연하다'처럼 부사형 '확연히'로 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '뚜렷하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used mostly for differences and changes that stand out clearly. The adverb form '확연히' is very common, as in '확연히 달라지다' and '차이가 확연하다'. '뚜렷하다' is a similar word.

examples.en: No conclusive results have come out yet.

examples.ko: 그 소식은 확정적이지 않으니 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: That news isn't definite, so please wait.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 은퇴는 이미 확정적이라고 해요.
examples.en: They say that player's retirement is already as good as decided.

examples.ko: 확정적 증거가 없어서 조사를 계속하고 있어요.
examples.en: There is no conclusive evidence, so the investigation continues.
There isn't enough data to say it definitively.
If the schedule is definite, please let me know in advance.

explain: '확정적이다', '확정적인 + 명사' 형태로 써요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 '확정적 증거', '확정적 결과'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '정해졌어요', '확실해요'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as '확정적이다' or '확정적인 + noun'. You will often see it in news and reports, as in '확정적 증거' and '확정적 결과'. In daily conversation people say '정해졌어요' or '확실해요'.

examples.en: I put medicine on the affected area and wrapped it with a bandage.
The doctor examined the affected area.

examples.ko: 환부가 붓고 열이 나면 병원에 가세요.
examples.en: If the affected area swells and feels hot, go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 환부를 자꾸 만지면 더 나빠질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep touching the affected area, it can get worse.
Wash around the affected area with clean water.

examples.ko: 수술 뒤 환부가 아물 때까지 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful until the affected area heals after surgery.

explain: 병원이나 약 설명서에서 '환부에 바르세요'처럼 자주 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '아픈 데', '다친 데'라고 해요. '상처'는 다친 자국 자체를 말하고, 환부는 아프거나 다친 부위를 말해요.
explain_en: You often see it at hospitals and on medicine instructions, as in '환부에 바르세요'. In daily talk people say '아픈 데' or '다친 데'. '상처' is the wound itself, while 환부 is the sick or injured area.

examples.en: When the goal went in, the crowd cheered with joy.
The children burst into delighted cries at the sight of snow.
Shouts of joy burst out from all around.
I woke up startled by the sound of cheering.

examples.ko: 선물을 열어 본 동생이 환성을 올렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling cried out with joy after opening the present.
The cheers and applause went on for a long time.

explain: 기뻐서 지르는 소리에 쓰고, '환성을 지르다/터뜨리다/올리다'로 말해요. '함성'은 여러 사람이 크게 외치는 소리라서 꼭 기쁜 일만은 아니고, '비명'은 놀라거나 무서울 때 지르는 소리예요.
explain_en: It is a shout made out of joy, used in '환성을 지르다/터뜨리다/올리다'. '함성' is a loud shout by many people and is not necessarily happy, and '비명' is a scream from surprise or fear.

examples.ko: 그는 선물로 부모님의 환심을 사려고 했어요.
examples.en: He tried to win his parents' favor with a gift.

examples.ko: 환심을 사려고 일부러 칭찬하는 거 아니에요?
examples.en: Aren't you praising me on purpose to win my favor?
I won the child's favor with a single candy.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 사람들의 환심을 사는 데 능숙해요.
examples.en: That person is skilled at winning people over.

examples.ko: 비싼 선물로 환심을 사려는 건 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: Trying to buy someone's favor with expensive gifts isn't good.
I heard they even lied to win favor.

explain: 주로 '환심을 사다'라는 형태로만 써요. 상대에게 잘 보이려는 속셈이 느껴질 때가 많아서 좋은 뜻만은 아니에요. 비슷하게 '비위를 맞추다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 비싼 선물로 친구의 환심을 사려고 했어요.
phrases.en: He tried to win his friend's favor with an expensive gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사다'는 물건을 산다는 뜻이 아니라 '얻다'에 가까워요. 잘 보이려고 애쓰는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '사다' here does not mean buying something; it is closer to 'gain'. It suggests effort to get on someone's good side.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the single pattern '환심을 사다'. It often suggests an intention to make a good impression, so it is not always positive. A similar expression is '비위를 맞추다' (to humor someone).

examples.en: I watched the Olympic downhill event all night.
The downhill course was so steep that it was scary.
The eagle gliding down looked really cool.

examples.ko: 활강은 스키에서 가장 빠른 종목 중 하나예요.
examples.en: The downhill is one of the fastest events in skiing.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 활강 종목에서 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: That athlete won a gold medal in the downhill event.

examples.ko: 글라이더의 활강 거리를 직접 재 봤어요.
examples.en: I measured the glider's gliding distance myself.

explain: 스키의 '활강' 종목(다운힐)이 가장 흔하고, 새나 글라이더가 날개를 펴고 미끄러지듯 내려오는 것에도 써요. '활강 코스', '활강 경기'처럼 다른 명사와 붙어 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The most common use is the skiing event '활강' (downhill), but it also describes birds or gliders sliding down through the air with their wings spread. It often joins other nouns, as in '활강 코스' and '활강 경기'.

examples.en: The eagle glided down slowly and landed by the river.

examples.ko: 선수들이 눈 덮인 산을 빠르게 활강해요.
examples.en: The athletes speed down the snow-covered mountain.
The paraglider glided down riding the wind.
For beginners, it's safer to go down slowly.
I fell while skiing down the slope.

examples.ko: 안전하게 활강하려면 먼저 장비를 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: To go down safely, you first need to check your equipment.

explain: 스키뿐 아니라 새나 글라이더가 공중에서 미끄러지듯 내려올 때도 써요. 일상 대화에서 스키 이야기는 '스키를 타고 내려오다'라고도 말해요. 보통 속도감 있게 내려오는 모습을 그릴 때 어울려요.
explain_en: Besides skiing, it is used when birds or gliders slide down through the air. In everyday talk about skiing, people may also say '스키를 타고 내려오다'. It suits scenes of coming down with a sense of speed.

examples.en: My younger sibling is outgoing, so they have many friends.
She's such a lively kid that she makes friends anywhere quickly.
My grandmother is very energetic for her age.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 활달하게 웃는 모습이 매력적이에요.
examples.en: That actor's cheerful, open smile is charming.
The new teacher is outgoing and kind.
I was quiet as a child, but now I've become outgoing.

explain: 밝고 씩씩하게 사람을 대하는 성격을 말할 때 써요. '활발하다'와 비슷하지만 활발하다는 '활발한 토론'처럼 활동이나 분위기에도 쓰고, 활달하다는 주로 사람의 성격에 써요. 반대는 '내성적이다', '소극적이다'예요.
explain_en: It describes a bright, lively personality that deals with people confidently. It is close to '활발하다', but 활발하다 also applies to activities and atmosphere (as in '활발한 토론'), while 활달하다 is mainly for a person's character. Opposites are '내성적이다' (introverted) and '소극적이다' (passive).
